SpaceX just bought your code editor for $60 billion.

Cursor — the AI-native coding tool used by engineering teams worldwide — was acquired by SpaceX in an all-stock deal filed June 16. The numbers: $4 billion in annualized revenue. $2.6 billion from enterprise.

But the real story is what comes next. A joint AI model trained on xAI's Colossus supercomputer will ship inside Cursor and a new product called Grok Build. That means the tool your developers write code in will be directly connected to one of the largest private AI compute clusters ever built.

The IDE used to be a neutral workspace. Now it is becoming a vertically integrated AI platform — tied to specific models, specific training data, and specific infrastructure.

For technical leaders, this changes the calculus on developer tooling entirely. The code editor is no longer a utility. It is a strategic dependency. And the companies behind these tools are making bets that go far beyond writing software.

Nasdaq-100 inclusion is expected by July 7. Five of six analysts covering the deal recommend buying. Closing expected Q3 2026.
